question: True or false: a lamp scoring 95 out of 100 on the colour rendering index can still turn skin wrong on camera?
answer: True. The standard index averages how eight pale, pastel test colours look under the lamp, judged by a model of the human eye. Saturated reds are left out of that average, and camera sensors respond differently from eyes. In 2016 the film Academy presented a Spectral Similarity Index built for cameras instead.
move: Before trusting a score, ask which cases were averaged to make it.
ask: Which score do I trust without asking which cases were averaged to produce it?
trap: Trusting a high score without asking what the test sampled.
